record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: If M is an asymptotically flat 3-manifold with non-negative scalar curvature and Sigma is a stable minimal 2-sphere in M, can one prove the Penrose inequality area(Sigma) <= 16 pi (ADM mass)^2, and can this inequality be generalized to initial data sets that are not time symmetric?

evidence.quote: Let M be a 3-manifold, AF with non-negative scalar curvature, and let :E c M be a stable minimal2-sphere. Prove the Penrose inequality [PRl] area(:E) ~ l61t (mass)2 where mass is the ADM mass of M. This would give an upper bound on the area of an apparent horizon in a time-symmetric data set. Find a generalisation of this inequality to initial data sets which are not time-symmetric.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, complete, asymptotically flat Riemannian 3-manifold with non-negative scalar curvature. Recall that $(M,g)$ is asymptotically flat if, outside a compact set, $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$ minus a ball and, in the corresponding coordinates $(x^i)$, the metric satisfies $g_{ij} = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-1})$ with appropriate decay on derivatives, and the ADM mass
$$m_{ADM}(M,g) \;=\; \frac{1}{16\pi}\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}\sum_{i,j}(\partial_i g_{ij}-\partial_j g_{ii})\,\nu^j\,dA$$
is finite, where $S_r$ is the coordinate sphere of radius $r$ and $\nu$ its outward unit normal.

Let $\Sigma\subset M$ be a stable minimal 2-sphere (a smooth embedded 2-sphere with zero mean curvature and non-negative second variation of area).

(a) Prove the Penrose inequality
$$\operatorname{area}(\Sigma)\;\le\;16\pi\,m_{ADM}(M,g)^2.$$

(b) Formulate and prove a generalization of this inequality to (non-time-symmetric) initial data sets $(M,g,K)$, where $K$ is a symmetric 2-tensor on $M$ playing the role of the second fundamental form of $M$ in a putative spacetime, $(g,K)$ satisfies the dominant energy condition, and the role of $\Sigma$ is played by an outermost (stable) marginally outer trapped 2-sphere.
artifact.status_search_result: The time-symmetric (Riemannian) Penrose inequality with the stated sharp constant was proved by Huisken–Ilmanen (2001, single-component horizon, via inverse mean curvature flow) and by Bray (2001, multiple components, via conformal flow), so part (a) is solved in the case where the stable minimal sphere is the outermost horizon. The general spacetime Penrose inequality for non-time-symmetric initial data sets (part (b)) remains open in full generality; recent work (e.g., spacetime Penrose inequality with suboptimal constant, 2025; cohomogeneity-one cases, 2024) has produced partial results but not the sharp inequality.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Penrose inequality - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Proved by Huisken–Ilmanen (2001) and Bray (2001) in the Riemannian (time-symmetric) case.
status_evidence.claim: The Riemannian Penrose inequality is solved.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the Spacetime Penrose Inequality With Suboptimal Constant
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes a Penrose-type mass lower bound for asymptotically flat/hyperboloidal initial data with dominant energy condition, but with a suboptimal constant.
status_evidence.claim: The sharp spacetime Penrose inequality is still open; only suboptimal versions are known.

status_evidence.title: Present status of the Penrose inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the status of the Penrose inequality, indicating the general spacetime case remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The spacetime/general Penrose inequality remains open.
